title: a quota error with a scheduled reset resumes the same runtime instead of failing over
proves: a worker exhaustion envelope with error code quota_exhausted and a resetAt strictly inside the node's own deadline classifies as a scheduled reset (quotaResetSchedule in backoff.mjs finds resetAt in the future and before the deadline), so classifyTransition returns kind:"reset" rather than "failover": planRoute keeps the current runtime and charges no failover hop, the node waits out the backoff and is re-dispatched on the same runtime, and it finishes on the invocation the recording queued next — proving the run resumed the attempt instead of spending the runtime's declared fallback. The replay driver's own canonicalError now preserves resetAt exactly as a real provider envelope would carry it (see replay.mjs's canonicalError), which is what makes this branch reachable through replay at all; the recorded resetAt below is the relative placeholder "+3000" (three seconds from whenever the case is materialized), resolved to a real timestamp by the eval harness before the replay driver ever sees it.

contract.goal: prove a quota error with a scheduled reset resumes the same runtime instead of failing over
